_comment: ── HISTORY: the react-router entries (removed 2026-08-23) ────────────────
They bypassed GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 as 'no patched version exists for React
18'. Correct when written; already false when removed — the advisory had
been re-scoped, making the pinned react-router 7.18.2 the 7.x patch. The
gate had been passing on its own merits, not on the bypass.
The lesson: a bypass records a judgement about the world at a point in
time, and advisories get re-scoped. Re-read before renewing.
1. CLAUDE.md recorded netlify-cli as un-bumpable past 27.1.2 because
@netlify/dev@5.0.4 required @netlify/ai@^1.0.1, which had never been
published — the floating transitive range that killed a production
deploy. It has since shipped. Re-checking instead of trusting the note
moved the pin 27.1.2 -> 27.4.2, which resolved 2 of 7 high advisories
(extract-zip path traversal) and made the tree 388 packages smaller.
2. The gate itself audited ONLY the repo root, so it never saw this tree
at all — a blind spot on the exact lockfile that runs with production
deploy credentials. check-vulnerabilities.mjs now audits both. That is
why these five entries appear now and did not before: they were always
there, nothing was looking.
⚠️ approvedBy is 'pending-owner-review' — these entries were authored in a
coding session and need the repo owner's explicit sign-off. A bypass is a
risk acceptance, and that is not a decision an assistant gets to make.

bypasses.reason: netlify dev's image-transform chain (netlify-cli -> @netlify/dev -> @netlify/images -> ipx -> sharp -> libvips). This repo installs that tree for ONE purpose — `netlify deploy` in phase-gate.yml — and never runs `netlify dev`. VERIFIED, not assumed: with node_modules/@img and node_modules/sharp removed from an otherwise complete `npm ci --ignore-scripts` install, `netlify --version` succeeds, `netlify deploy --help` succeeds (loading the deploy command's own module graph — the check the workflow already runs before touching production), and `netlify deploy` reaches its own argument validation. The libvips CVEs require decoding attacker-controlled image input; the deploy step uploads an already-built directory and decodes nothing. NOTE: --ignore-scripts does NOT keep libvips off disk — modern sharp ships prebuilt binaries as optional dependencies, not a postinstall download. The earlier draft of this reason claimed otherwise and was wrong. npm offers exactly one remedy: netlify-cli 23.13.5, a MAJOR DOWNGRADE of the one tool that publishes production, which is the larger risk.
bypasses.todo: TODO: drop this bypass when sharp publishes a libvips bump that @netlify/images picks up, or when Netlify decouples image transforms from the CLI's default tree. Re-read the advisories on expiry — do not renew on the strength of this note (see the react-router entries that went stale before anyone re-checked them).
